title: COINPOUR / FROZEN FLOW ILLUSION
core_formula: familiar objects -> concealed support -> freeze a familiar action -> hide engineering in the visual story -> impossible-looking collectible
summary: A cup, saucer, bent fork and real coins form a frozen pouring illusion where concealed support disappears inside the visual story.
learn: Ask what action the object normally performs.
Explore whether that action can be frozen into a physical object.
Static objects can feel mid-action when the critical moment is captured.
Use story elements to hide the engineering.
Many small objects can become one large gesture.
Space itself can become part of the object.
Ordinary materials can create premium visual impact through spatial organization.
avoid: coins as the only valid flowing material
saucers, forks or gold-trimmed ceramics as fixed ingredients
floating tableware as a repetitive trope
support that remains too visually obvious
failure_modes: the fork/support is too visible and the illusion collapses immediately
the action does not read clearly as pouring
the coin stream feels like random clutter instead of one gesture
the gap between cup and saucer is too small to create suspension
the piece feels like a craft trick rather than a refined collectible object
too much material or too many coins flatten the silhouette and weaken the illusion
source: user-provided concept text + 3 images for CONCEPT 08
